texts.preamble: Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November, 2020 Author: Alok Mathur Bench: Alok Mathur High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Court No. - 29 Case :- U/S 482/378/407 No. - 2631 of 2020 Applicant :- Chandan Singh Verma Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. & Anr. Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Asarey Verma Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Alok Mathur,J. 1.
texts.facts: 2. By means of the present applicant the applicant has sought quashing the criminal proceedings of Case No.14 of 2020 (State Vs. Chandan Singh Verma) under Section 18 (a)/28 and 18 (c)/27(b) II of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, Police Station Neemgaon, District Lakhimpur Kheri as well as the summoning order dated 29.1.2020. According to the applicant a raid was conducted on 13.7.2018 at the said medical store by a team consisting of police officials as well as officials of Drugs and Cosmetics Department, State of U.P. and it was found that the applicant was conducting the Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11523761/ 1 business in selling drugs and cosmetics without proper license nor was he able to produce any such license to the raiding party. It was stated that despite a notice having been issued to him earlier, he could not submit any document for running his business during the said raid. It has been submitted that the drugs being sold by him were also seized in accordance with the rules framed therein. Thereafter an F.I.R. was registered on 13.7.2018 in case crime No.190 of 2018, under Sections- 419, 420 of IPC and 18 (A), 18 (c), 27 (b) (ii), 28 of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 at police station Neemgaon, District Lakhimpur Kheri.
texts.arguments: 3. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicant is running a medical store styled as M/s Verma Medical Store, Bhupatipur Road, Gadariya, Chauraha, Police Station - Neemgaon, Distric Kheri. 4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that his grievance for which he has approached this Court is with regard to the proceedings initiated by the State in pursuance of the complaint moved by Drug Inspector, Food Safety and Drug Administration, Office of District Magistrate, Lakhimpur Kheri wherein it has been mentioned that the premises of the applicant was raided on 13.7.2018 in which it was found that the applicant was conducting the business without any license and further that on the said date certain drugs mentioned in para 7 of Annexure No.2 were seized. The drugs were further sent to the State Public Analysis Laboratory, U.P. Aliganj, Lucknow which has reported that the said drugs were adulterated and, therefore, as a consequence of the said complaint criminal proceedings and summoning order dated 29.1.2020, which have been impugned in the present case, have been issued. The only ground urged by the applicant is that prosecution on the same set of facts has been taken on the basis of an F.I.R., then proceedings in the compliant case should not have been undertaken and this is violative of Article 20 of the Constitution of India and, therefore, has prayed that the present proceedings b [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5. Learned A.G.A., on the hand, has vehemently opposed the petition and submitted that facts in both cases are very different and the offence under which the applicant has been charged are different and, therefore, there is no basis for allowing the petition of the petitioner. Aforesaid Sections provide as under:-" "18 (c) Manufacture for sale or for distribution, or sell, or stock or exhibit or offer for sale or distribute any drug or cosmetic, except under and in accordance with the conditions of a license issued for such purpose under this Chapter: 18-A. Disclosure of the name of the manufacture, etc.:- Every person, not being the manufacturer of a drug or cosmetic or his agent for the distribution thereof, shall, if so required, disclose to the Inspector the name, address and other particulars of the person from whom he acquired the drug or cosmetic. 27. Penalty for manufacture, sale, etc., of drugs in contravention of this Chapter: Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11523761/ 2 (b) any drug (i) .......or (ii) without a valid license as required under clause (c) of section 18, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees or three times the value of the drugs confiscated, whichever is more." 28. Penalty for non-disclosure of the name of the manufacturer, etc.:- Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 18-A [or section 24] shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty thousand rupees or with both." 8.
